---
title: "Animations"
description-meta: "Interactive pictures of supersingular isogeny graphs: random walks, growing balls, and the spectral law of Hecke operators."
---

Pictures of the supersingular isogeny graphs I work on: $G_p(2)$, $G_p(\{2,3\})$ and $G_p(\{2,3,5\})$ for primes up to 20011, and graphs with level structure $\Gamma_0(5)$, $\Gamma_1(5)$, $\Gamma(2)$ and $\Gamma(4)$ (including a disconnected one). Every graph is computed from scratch (arithmetic in $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$ and Vélu's formulas, with consistency checks). Each picture can be shown as the full graph, its $\mathbb{F}_p$-subgraph, or its quotient by Frobenius, and the menu under it switches from the plain **graph viewer** to the animations below.

[Random walks](walks.qmd)
: A random walk, drawn as a laser with a fading trail.

[Blooming](balls.qmd)
: A ball grows around a random curve until it collides with itself and closes a cycle (*blooming for collision*), or until it contains a Frobenius conjugate pair, or in the quotient by Frobenius collides with itself or reaches the $\mathbb{F}_p$-subgraph (*blooming for conjugates*). The second takes about $\sqrt{n}$ vertices.

[Spectral law](spectral.qmd)
: The eigenvalues of the Hecke operator $T_\ell$ on $S_2(\Gamma_0(p))$ approach the Kesten–McKay law as $p \to \infty$ (about 100 primes up to 20011).

[Read more](about.qmd)
: Exact definitions: the graphs and their level structures, Frobenius on vertices and edges, the $\mathbb{F}_p$-subgraph (spine) with pictures, the quotient by Frobenius, and the spectral law. The eye in the corner of each picture links here.
